messages.content: New work trip after Boise: Louisville-area bottling plant. I need a flight and hotel shortlist for a Tuesday Oct. 7 morning operator walk-through. There is a distributor dinner Monday evening and maybe a Wednesday pricing session in Lexington.

Got it. For the flight, are you trying to arrive Monday before dinner, or are you open to a Sunday arrival if that protects Tuesday better? Also, SFO only or any Bay Area airport if the routing is cleaner?
SFO first, OAK acceptable if it is clearly better. Arrive into SDF with enough cushion for dinner Monday, and do not give me a drawn-out connection. One stop is fine.
Understood. For hotels, should I look closest to the plant in Jeffersontown/east Louisville, near SDF for easier arrival and departure, or compare both?
Compare Jeffersontown, Louisville east end, and airport. Good guest feedback, parking, practical room setup, and not isolated for dinner. No downtown unless it is somehow the obvious answer.
I’ll treat downtown as out unless everything else fails. For the uncertain Lexington piece, should I price the base stay through Tuesday checkout and show the Tuesday-night add-on separately?
Yes. If I leave Sunday, base hotel is Sunday and Monday nights. If I leave Monday, base hotel is Monday only. Price the Tuesday night separately, but don’t hold it yet.

Flight shortlist into SDF: best protection is Delta SFO-MSP-SDF on Sunday Oct. 5, departing about 12:35 p.m. and arriving around 10:18 p.m., with a roughly 1 hr 40 min MSP connection. It adds a hotel night but gives all day Monday for prep and dinner. Acceptable Monday backup is United SFO-ORD-SDF, about 6:10 a.m. to 3:02 p.m., one ORD connection around 1 hr 35 min. It works only if everything runs on time. I would avoid later Monday options landing after 5 p.m.
How bad is the Sunday late arrival? I do not want to be dragging on Monday if I can avoid it.

It is late but manageable: land about 10:18 p.m., rental-car pickup and drive to east Louisville is roughly 25 to 30 minutes if bags are quick, so hotel arrival around 11:15. The trade-off is much better Monday control. The Monday morning option saves the room night, but any delay pushes directly into dinner logistics.
Okay. Hotel options?

Best fit: Drury Inn & Suites Louisville East in the Jeffersontown/east Louisville area, about 4.5 Google rating, free parking, listed fridge/microwave and in-room coffee, and several dinner options along Hurstbourne/Shelbyville. Usually around $158-$172 per night on flexible rates. Backup in the same zone: Hilton Garden Inn Louisville East, about 4.2 rating, free parking, on-site restaurant, and a more conventional business-hotel setup. Airport-area backup: Hampton Inn Louisville Airport/Fair Expo Center, about 4.3 rating and easiest for SDF, but farther from the plant and less useful for Monday dinner.
I don’t need airport convenience if it makes Monday worse. Is Jeffersontown decent for dinner?

Yes. The Jeffersontown/east Louisville corridor is much better for Monday evening: chain and local restaurants within a short drive, easier access to the plant side, and no need to backtrack from the airport. The airport hotel is simpler only on arrival night and departure day.
What about the Lexington add-on? If it happens it is probably Wednesday at 10 a.m.

Two clean options: book the base Drury stay for Sunday and Monday only, then add Tuesday night once Lexington is confirmed; or hold a separate cancellable Tuesday night now and cancel it if the pricing session moves remote. Since you asked not to hold it yet, I’d note the Tuesday-night Drury rate and also check Lexington hotels later if the meeting is confirmed.
Don’t hold the extra night yet. I just need the option noted.

Noted. My recommendation is Sunday Delta via MSP plus Drury Inn & Suites Louisville East for Sunday and Monday nights on a flexible rate. The Monday United via ORD itinerary is the acceptable backup if the extra hotel night becomes a budget issue, but it is weaker for schedule protection.
Assume Tuesday evening return if Lexington drops. If Lexington happens, I might fly back Wednesday from LEX or SDF, whichever is less annoying.

Base return option: Delta SDF-DTW-SFO Tuesday Oct. 7, departing around 5:30 p.m. and arriving SFO around 10:10 p.m., with one reasonable DTW connection after the plant walk-through and debrief. If Lexington happens, I’d compare Wednesday afternoon LEX one-stop options against driving back to SDF; LEX may be cleaner if the meeting is actually in Lexington.
Good. Send me the concise version I can paste to the distributor. No booking.

Saved, not booked. Louisville shortlist: best-fit travel plan is Sunday Oct. 5 Delta SFO-MSP-SDF, afternoon departure with one manageable connection, arriving SDF about 10:18 p.m.; hotel lead is Drury Inn & Suites Louisville East for Sunday and Monday nights, flexible rate, strong guest feedback, free parking, practical room setup, and easy dinner access in Jeffersontown/east Louisville. Backup flight is Monday early United SFO-ORD-SDF, arriving about 3:02 p.m., but it leaves less cushion for Monday evening. Tuesday-night hotel and Wednesday return are not being held until the Lexington pricing session is confirmed.

messages.content: Update on Louisville: the distributor says I need to physically check the demo crates by late Monday afternoon. Recompare the Sunday afternoon arrival against the Monday early flight. I don’t love paying for Sunday night, but I can’t have the crates become a fire drill.

That makes the Sunday plan the safer choice. Delta SFO-MSP-SDF on Sunday still lands late, but it gives you Monday morning and afternoon in Louisville. The Monday United via ORD option arrives around 3:00 p.m. only if everything is on time; after bags, rental car, and the drive, the crate check would be tight.
Is there any Monday option that gets me there before 1 p.m. without being ridiculous?

Not a good one from SFO. The earlier Monday routings are pre-dawn departures and still tend to land midafternoon, or they introduce a less comfortable connection. I would not count on them for a late-afternoon in-person crate check.
Okay, lean Sunday. Now hotel: Drury in Jeffersontown versus the Hampton by the airport. Which actually makes the trip easier?

Drury Louisville East is better for the work days: stronger guest feedback, free parking, lots of dinner choices nearby, and a shorter drive toward the plant. Hampton Airport is easier at 10:30 p.m. Sunday and again on departure day, but it pushes Monday and Tuesday into longer drives.
Is Drury okay for a late Sunday check-in?

Yes, it should be fine. I’d add a late-arrival note and keep the reservation on a flexible rate. If you want the simplest possible arrival night, Hampton wins, but then Monday crate check and dinner logistics are worse.
Then keep Drury as the lead. What do you recommend on the Lexington question now?

I’d still avoid booking the Tuesday night until the pricing meeting is firm. Book Drury Sunday and Monday nights only. If Lexington is confirmed, add Tuesday night either at Drury or near Lexington depending on where the Wednesday meeting lands. That keeps the base trip clean and avoids paying for a speculative extra night.
And the Tuesday return if Lexington drops?

Delta SDF-DTW-SFO around 5:30 p.m. Tuesday remains the best fit. It gives you room after the operator walk-through and distributor debrief, with one reasonable connection. United via ORD is an acceptable backup, but the connection quality is not better enough to beat the Delta schedule.
Use the Delta package unless the fare jumps. Window seat later if seat selection is open, but do not book yet. I need client approval.

Saved, still not booked. Current recommendation: Delta SFO-MSP-SDF Sunday Oct. 5 afternoon departure, arriving about 10:18 p.m.; Drury Inn & Suites Louisville East for Sunday and Monday nights on a flexible rate with late-arrival note; Delta SDF-DTW-SFO Tuesday Oct. 7 around 5:30 p.m. The Monday early flight is now only a budget-driven backup because it is too tight for the crate check. No Tuesday-night Lexington hold unless the client confirms the Wednesday session.
